# efema

> A sync relay for local-first apps: it keeps changes in order and cannot read them

Devices append batches of sealed entries to named streams, in the space their
access key opens; the relay gives them positions, links them into a hash chain
and hands every device what came after its cursor. It answers only its own
machine and HTTPS through a reverse proxy, holds each key to limits it
announces, and never decodes, merges or judges an entry. Five crates: the wire
format (`efema-proto`), the relay (`efema-server`), the client library that
compresses and seals every entry on the device and keeps it there until the
relay has it - or keeps the stream in an S3 bucket itself, with no relay at
all (`efema`), the sealing itself (`lacodda-seal`) and the proxy that
tears connections in the tests (`lacodda-tear`); `examples/mini-vault` is an
app built on the client. The repository was
started by [lyrn](https://github.com/lacodda/lyrn) as its `workspace` form;
`lyrn.toml` says which revision of the lacodda line's standard it carries.
Everything below is written for people and agents alike: there is no second set
of instructions kept elsewhere.
